statement: Let 51/100 ≤ a ≤ 1, 0 < e ≤ 10−3, and take xr = a + 16e, wr = 1 − a − 6e, zr = 17/50. Choose P0 sufficiently large in terms of e and the fixed data. For U, T1 ≥ 1 and a sixth-power-free row u with (u, S) = 1 and qu ≍ U, let ψ∗ u be the primitive character inducing χ•(u). Let Wu be any subset of {w : ℜw = wr, |ℑw| ≤ T1}. Suppose ψ∗ u is nonprincipal and, uniformly for w ∈ Wu, |L(1 − w, ψ∗ u)| ≪ Uϵ with any prescribed small power. For this row on the displayed dynamic region, define Bi by its preceding slot sum, interpreting each Bp as Gp/Hp, with Gp from Equation (16.2). The stated choice of P0 makes Hp ̸= 0 there for every slot prime, as proved at the start of the proof. This statement asserts individual continuation only on this dynamic region. Define the main and error parts of a slot by Qi(u; z) = − X p∈Pi(Z) Wi(qp/Pi)qz−1 p χp(u), Di(u) = Bi(u; x, w, z) − Qi(u; z).
